text:
morgan: heads up — canary rollout of runtime v2.4.3 started ~10:05 UTC, we’re seeing p99 jump for text-gen routes from ~110ms -> ~420ms for a handful of tenants. raising here for triage.
infra-bot: alert: p99 latency spike detected on /generate (route: text-gen). cohort sample id=cohort-24. Canary traffic: 10% since 10:05 UTC. See logs: https://logs.redwood.local/streams/abc123 :warning:
lee: ack. which models/cohorts affected? any auth errors or 5xx coupling?
morgan: mainly gpt-small-ish cust models (gpt-neo family). no 5xx, just long tail. token rates look normal. span traces show lots of time in "kernel_select" + queueing at hotpath.
sanika: can you paste an example trace id? will try reproduce locally with synthetic replay.
morgan: trace id 20260317-xyz. snippet: "kernel_select: 210ms, batch_wait: 120ms, compute: 60ms, kv_cache_lookup: 15ms"
lee: hmm kernel_select up from ~5ms baseline. we recently flipped default kernel selector heuristic in v2.4.3 to favor fused kernels for longer sequences.
sanika: hypothesis: selector is choosing a suboptimal kernel for short sequences and adding scheduling cost. repro steps I'm running:
```
# synthetic replay using stressproxy
stressproxy replay --cohort cohort-24 --routes /generate --concurrency 40 --duration 2m --model gpt-neo-1.3b --runtime v2.4.3
```
let me know if you want me to run different flags.
lee: try forcing selector back to old heuristic on a single canary host: `KERNEL_SELECTOR=legacy` and restart runtime binary. also check `--prefer-single-stream-kernels` toggle.
morgan: toggled legacy selector on one canary machine (host canary-7), restarted runtime. immediate effect: p99 on that host dropped to ~120ms in the synthetic run. other canaries still high.
oncall: good repro. mitigation options:
• roll back selector change in v2.4.3 and re-deploy canary
• split traffic away from affected canaries
• temporary routing rule to prefer older runtime version for cohort-24
• adjust selector config remotely if exposed
customer-success: flagged a customer (acct: atlas-inc) who reported slow UX. they’re on cohort-24; notified them we're triaging and will mitigate.
lee: let's do a targeted config patch: push remote override `kernel_selector=legacy` via config service to all canaries, validate, then either keep and backfill or rollback binary change in next release.
sanika: applying config override now via /config-service PATCH. command: `curl -X PATCH https://config.internal/api/runtime/canary -d '{"kernel_selector":"legacy"}'` (in flight)
infra-bot: config change applied to canary pool at 10:20 UTC. change id cfg-789
morgan: monitoring — p99 across canary pool trending down to ~130-150ms within 90s of change. customer CS updated.
customer-success: thx — they confirmed improvement in a quick check. :tada:
lee: next steps: (1) open a follow-up PR to revert the heuristic in runtime repo and add more conservative heuristics + testing (2) add unit/regression test that runs selector on representative short/long seq matrix (3) create runbook snippet to opt a cohort out via config override quickly (4) postmortem with timeline + root cause.
sanika: filing replay artifacts + traces in ticket: https://pm.redwood.local/issue/RUNTIME-1422
morgan: adding to incident board. will schedule rollback PR if config override shows intermittent cases. overall mitigation done for now. thanks all.
oncall: if anything regresses, @oncall please escalate and we'll roll traffic.
lee: noted. assigning owners: lee (root cause/PR), sanika (replay + test), morgan (customer comms + postmortem)
morgan: closing thread for now — will update when PR lands. :white_check_mark:
